translation_notes: EXCLUDED because it cannot be executed, not because of the notation: the region is a SQLAlchemy/Virtuoso integration test whose assertions read triples back out of a live Virtuoso server over ODBC after it has materialised them from SQL rows through a quad-map declaration. It needs that server plus sqlalchemy, pyodbc, nose and sqla_rdfbridge (none installed; virtuoso-python is Python-2 era) and the surrounding TestMapping class with the declarative classes A/B/C/D. Standing that in would fabricate the result rather than compare the two representations; the driver still emits a canonical verdict carrying the exact import failure

the translation itself is a clean notation change and was verified to transpile: TST.safe_name / TST.name become tst:safe_name / tst:name (checked to yield URIRef('http://example.com/test#safe_name') etc.), and TST = Namespace('http://example.com/test#') is replaced by @prefix tst:
the draft had inserted the @prefix line INSIDE the parenthesised 'from virtuoso.vmapping import (...)' list, which is not a statement position and does not transpile; it is moved after the import
the two remaining tst: uses are read patterns - graph.triples((None, tst:safe_name, None)) - so the island only replaces term construction here, as in the other read-only regions

NOTE for the whole source file: TST is also consumed as nsm.bind('tst', TST) and as getattr(TST, 'col_pattern_%s_%s' % ...), i.e. a runtime object and a dynamically computed local name; @prefix can serve neither, so a whole-file translation would keep the Namespace binding alongside the declaration
